proposal:
Proposal: Solvent-Free Synthesis of Porous Cu-BTC MOF (HKUST-1) for Sustainable CO2 Capture

Research Goal: We propose a modified green, solvent-free synthesis of Cu-BTC (HKUST-1) using ethanol as a less toxic alternative washing solvent to methanol.

Demo Revision Request applied: {feedback}

[Need & Background]
Global climate change driven by rising greenhouse gas emissions necessitates efficient carbon capture technologies. HKUST-1 (Cu-BTC) is promising for CO2 adsorption but conventional solvothermal synthesis requires hazardous organic solvents.

[Solution]
A solvent-free mechanochemical coordination approach: dry-grinding copper(II) nitrate trihydrate and BTC (1.5:1 molar ratio) for 15 minutes, then heating in a sealed autoclave at 120 degC for 3 hours. Unreacted starting materials are removed via centrifugal washing with ethanol instead of methanol.

[Differentiation]
Produces HKUST-1 with relative crystallinity up to 130% compared to commercial standards in just 3 hours at 120 degC, while utilizing low-toxicity ethanol instead of methanol for purification.

[Benefit]
Reduces the E-factor of MOF production and adopts green ethanol for purification; CO2 adsorption capacity of 1.7 mmol/g at 30 degC and 1 bar.

[Experimental Overview]
Synthesize the Cu-BTC framework by dry grinding, followed by heating at 120 degC for 3 hours. Activate and purify by centrifugal washing with ethanol and dry overnight at 80 degC under vacuum.
